The adverb carries the stress when it is fronted: FORTUNATELY, the audit found nothing. In mid-position it is usually unstressed.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Adverbs: Types and Position.

Decide the type first, then the position: manner at the end, frequency in the middle, time at either end, comment at the front with a comma. Never put an adverb between the verb and its object: she speaks English well, not she speaks well English.

manner — end, after the verb or object: he spoke quietly
frequency — mid-position: she rarely misses a deadline
time — end or front: we met yesterday / yesterday we met
comment — front with a comma: fortunately, the audit found nothing
degree — before the adjective or adverb: the results were surprisingly strong
linking adverb — front with a comma: however, the data was incomplete
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'She has ___ finished the report.'
2. Which position suits a comment adverb?
options: Between the verb and the object.

elements.content: 3. Which sentence is correct?
Read and listen: three examples in context.

She rarely misses a deadline. — Frequency before the main verb. (Mid-position.)
He spoke quietly and left. — Manner after the verb. (End position.)
Fortunately, the audit found nothing. — Comment on the whole clause. (Front position.)
What do you observe?

Adverbs fall into types that prefer different positions. Manner adverbs go at the end (she spoke quietly) or after the object. Frequency adverbs take mid-position, before the main verb and after the auxiliary (she rarely misses, she has rarely missed). Time adverbs go at the end or the front. Comment adverbs, which judge the whole sentence, take the front position with a comma (fortunately, admittedly).
1. Where does a frequency adverb go with an auxiliary?
2. What position does a comment adverb take?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can describe people, places and actions with the adjective or adverb that fits.

Success criteria:
- I can put a manner adverb after the object.
- I can put a frequency adverb in mid-position.
- I can use a comment adverb at the front with a comma.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ She speaks well English (adverb between the verb and its object) → ✅ She speaks English well
❌ Rarely she misses a deadline (frequency adverb before the subject, no inversion) → ✅ She rarely misses a deadline
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

She answered the question calmly.
The board has never rejected a proposal.
Admittedly, the timetable was optimistic.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where order of adjectives carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
